<!-- All news items below this line -->
;International relations
*[[Positions on Jerusalem]]
**The [[Czech Republic]] recognizes [[West Jerusalem]] as [[Israel]]'s capital "in practice". [http://www.mzv.cz/jnp/en/issues_and_press/mfa_statements/x2017_12_06_mfa_statement_jerusalem.html (Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs)]
**[[Philippines|Philippine]] President [[Rodrigo Duterte]] expresses interest in moving his country's embassy from [[Tel Aviv]] to [[Jerusalem]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/1.827208 (''Haaretz'')]
*[[Greek–Turkish relations]]
**The [[President of Turkey]] embarks on a two-day state visit of [[Greece]].  [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]]'s [[démarche]] is a first in 65 years. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/dec/07/turkish-president-erdogan-to-make-landmark-visit-to-greece (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-greece-turkey-erdogan-treaty/greek-president-tells-turkeys-erdogan-no-treaty-revision-idUSKBN1E1186 (Reuters)]
*[[European migrant crisis]], [[Treaty on European Union]]
**The [[European Commission]] orders [[Poland]], the [[Czech Republic]] and [[Hungary]] to [[European Court of Justice|court]] over their refusal to incorporate more refugees. This is the third step in a process that may lead to fines and loss of the countries' [[Suffrage|voting right]]s in the European Union. [http://www.standaard.be/cnt/dmf20171207_03230108 (''De Standaard'')] [http://www.zeit.de/politik/ausland/2017-12/eu-kommission-verklagt-ungarn-tschechien-und-polen (''Die Zeit'')]
*[[Economic globalization]]
**Fifteen countries ask the [[World Trade Organization]] a mandate to negotiate [[Regulation|binding rules]] on [[e-commerce]], days after [[India]] turned down negotiations. [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/foreign-trade/pressure-on-india-as-15-countries-seek-e-commerce-talks-at-wto/articleshow/61972141.cms (''Economic Times'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Same-sex marriage in Australia]]
**The [[Parliament of Australia]] votes to make [[same-sex marriage]] legal in [[Australia]]. [http://www.theaustralian.com.au/national-affairs/politicsnow-ssm-bill-decided-today-citizenship-saga-continues/news-story/642ba787fcb52a24f08d61be8ac650d7 (''The Australian'')]
*[[2017 Aztec High School shooting]]
**Three people, including the gunman, are killed in a school shooting at [[Aztec High School]] in [[New Mexico]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/crime/sheriff-3-dead-in-new-mexico-school-shooting/ar-BBGmBdU?&ocid=ientp (MSN)]
*[[2016–17 purges in Turkey]]
**[[Peoples' Democratic Party (Turkey)|Peoples’ Democratic Party]]’s co-chair [[Selahattin Demirtaş]] remains behind bars until the next hearing, scheduled for February 14, 2018. He risks 142 years in prison. [https://turkeypurge.com/court-rules-keep-pro-kurdish-opposition-leader-selahattin-demirtas-behind-bars (''Turkey Purge'')]
*Aftermath of the [[AMIA bombing]]
**In a 491-page ruling, a court indicts former [[President of Argentina]] [[Cristina Fernández]] for treason and orders for her arrest for "trying to cover up Iran's possible role in the 1994 bombing of a Jewish [[Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina|community center]] that killed 85 people". Former [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship|foreign affairs minister]] [[Héctor Timerman]] is also concerned. Both have previously denied wrongdoing. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-argentina-fernandez/argentinas-fernandez-charged-with-treason-judge-orders-arrest-idUSKBN1E11Q4 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2017 United States political sexual scandals]]
**United States Senator [[Al Franken]] announces that he will resign "in the coming weeks" amid sexual harassment allegations. [http://time.com/5053057/al-franken-resigns-senate-seat-minnesota/ (''Time'')]
**Arizona Congressman [[Trent Franks]] announces that he will resign on January 31, 2018. This announcement comes after two of his employees filed a complaint about his conduct, and the [[House Ethics Committee]] opened a sexual harassment investigation. [http://www.foxnews.com/politics/2017/12/07/rep-trent-franks-r-ariz-expected-to-resign.html (Fox News)]
*[[Nepalese legislative election, 2017]]
**Voters in [[Nepal]] go to the polls for the second round of a historic legislative election. The turnout is 67%, up from 65% in the first round. [https://www.foreignaffairs.com/articles/nepal/2017-12-07/election-nepal-decades-making (''Foreign Affairs'')] [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/world-news/nepal-clocks-67-voter-turnout-in-final-phase-of-historic-poll/articleshow/61970116.cms (''Economic Times'')]
*[[Cabinet of Germany]]
**The [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|Social Democratic Party]] congress votes to start talks on "whether and in what form" to support a new federal government. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/the-latest-german-social-democrats-back-talks-on-government/2017/12/07/54ec7fa6-db79-11e7-a241-0848315642d0_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Politics of Poland]]
**[[Poland|Polish]] Prime Minister [[Beata Szydło]] resigns just hours after surviving an opposition no-confidence motion. She will be replaced by [[Ministry of Finance (Poland)|Finance Minister]] [[Mateusz Morawiecki]], according to the ruling [[Law and Justice (Poland)|Law and Justice]] party. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-42272808 (BBC)]

;Sports
*[[UEFA Euro 2020]]
**[[Eurostadium]] in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]], is unselected as a host for the [[UEFA Euro]] 2020 football competition, ceding its place for group stage matches to [[Wembley Stadium]] in [[London]], [[England]]. [[Prime Minister of Belgium]] [[Charles Michel]] says the city made the error of wanting to build a stadium outside its territory. [http://www.voetbalnieuws.be/news/268000/kogel-door-de-kerk-uefa-heeft-beslist-over-eurostadion (''voetbalnieuws.be'')] [https://www.vrt.be/vrtnws/nl/2017/12/07/reynders-over-eurostadion---begrijp-niet-waarom-brussels-gewest-/ (VRT)]
